Plot a ranked summary of mean percent-of-control by treatment

Source: R/normalization.R
plot_treatment_summary.Rd

Summarizes normalize_to_control() output into one bar per treatment: the mean percent-of-control value across all concentrations and replicates, with a standard error bar, ranked from strongest to weakest effect. A quick way to rank an entire drug panel by response.

Usage

plot_treatment_summary(
  .data,
  treatment_column_name = "Treatment",
  control_treatment_name = "Control",
  compare_to_control = FALSE,
  stat_method = c("wilcox", "t.test"),
  p_adjust_method = "BH",
  pvalue_label = c("p.adj.signif", "p.signif", "p.adj.format", "p.format")
)

Arguments

.data

Data frame that has been through normalize_to_control() on the long format (must contain "pct_of_control", "marker_positivity" and a treatment column).

treatment_column_name

Column holding the treatment label. Defaults to "Treatment".

control_treatment_name

Value identifying control/vehicle wells, excluded from the summary. Defaults to "Control".

compare_to_control

Logical; whether to compute and annotate p-values comparing each treatment against control_treatment_name per marker facet. Defaults to FALSE.

stat_method

Statistical test used when compare_to_control = TRUE: "wilcox" (default) or "t.test".

p_adjust_method

Multiple-testing correction method passed to stats::p.adjust() across treatments within each marker facet. Supports "BH" (Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, default), "bonferroni", "holm", "fdr", "hochberg", "hommel", "BY", or "none".

pvalue_label

Format for p-value annotations: "p.adj.signif" (adjusted *, **, ***, ns, default), "p.signif" (unadjusted), "p.adj.format", or "p.format".

Value

A ggplot object (with attr(plot, "stats") populated when compare_to_control = TRUE).

Details

When multiple drug concentrations or imaged fields of view are present in .data, compare_to_control = TRUE pools all normalized observations for each treatment against control_treatment_name to test for an overall treatment effect across the tested condition. To test specific concentrations individually without pooling across doses, subset .data to a single concentration first or use get_QC_plots(..., x_plot_var = "Treatment_complete", compare_to_control = TRUE).

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  PID = "PID1",
  Treatment = c("Control", "Control", "DrugA", "DrugA", "DrugB", "DrugB"),
  marker_positivity = "cCASP3",
  marker_positivity_ratio = c(10, 10, 4, 6, 14, 16)
)
normalized <- normalize_to_control(df)
plot_treatment_summary(normalized)
